correctness.rationale: Acyclicity is a separate constraint on each cycle block, so the weight law factors across edge-disjoint blocks. A simple connecting path must traverse the unique block-cut route, and the resulting block demands suffice. On one shared cycle, after rescaling by the full-cycle weight, a nonempty missing set carries product weight in the reciprocals. The first event confines it to one row, the second to one column, and their intersection to one cell, giving exactly R,S,H after subtracting empty-set terms. As an algebra check, writing U=X+Y, one has Z=U+P+Q+XY+PY+QX+PQ and RS=U^2+UXY+QX^2+PY^2-4PQ, yielding the stated positive identity and strictness. Shared bridges have covariance p(1-p)>0. Every factor in the global product comparison is positive (a positive-weight local spanning tree satisfies both demands), so strictness is preserved exactly as claimed. For any shared cycle both partitions have two nonempty arcs, and a 2-by-2 support with no empty row or column contains a pair of opposite occupied cells; thus the criterion also simplifies to sharing any route block.
residual_risks: The source script checks the global nonnegative inequality on examples, not the entire global strictness criterion; the universal proof covers strictness. Zero or infinite weights and overlapping cycles are outside scope.
